title: Dispatching work
description: POST /v1/orchestrator/tasks and POST /v1/orchestrator/tasks/{id}/settle. The intent is recorded durably before the session is opened, so a crash between the two leaves a task that is known and unstarted rather than one running and unrecorded.

claims.description: The paths this task intends to write, declared before it starts. Absent is refused and an empty list is accepted: `I declared none` and `I did not say` are different requests, and only one of them can be arbitrated against another root. This is a dispatch-time reservation compared between roots, not filesystem enforcement — nothing stops a child writing outside it, and pretending otherwise would be the more dangerous lie.

task_id.description: Supply one to make the dispatch idempotent: the same id with the same body replays rather than starting a second session.

DispatchResult.description: The intent committed. It does not say the assistant received anything — that is a later fact with its own evidence, and `replayed` is how a caller tells a fresh dispatch from one it had already made.

SettleResult.description: Whether the task has written a result yet. `settled` false is not a failure; it means nothing has been written, which is the ordinary state of work still in progress.
